# Pharmaceuticals

This folder contains pharmaceutical products used in the treatment of atrial fibrillation in Denmark, specifically focusing on anticoagulation therapies. The pages detail the clinical use, safety profiles, and national quality database monitoring of both modern direct oral anticoagulants and classic warfarin-based treatments, highlighting their comparative risks of severe bleeding and ischemic stroke.

## Pages

- [[doac|DOAC]] — Direct oral anticoagulants (such as dabigatran, rivaroxaban, apixaban, and edoxaban) used to prevent ischemic stroke while minimizing bleeding risks, with national monitoring of renal function and adverse events.
- [[marevan]] — A classic oral anticoagulant (warfarin) frequently compared against DOACs in national clinical quality reports to evaluate treatment safety, severe bleeding rates, and stroke prevention efficacy.
